name: ReelBite Hollywood
tagline: Hollywood's biggest moments, cut down to 60 seconds.
about: English Shorts on true Hollywood stories (flops, behind-the-scenes, box office, studio drama), 60-90 s, told like a comic explainer but with real proof on screen: free-licence photos (Wikimedia Commons, credited), headline and quote cards with sources, animated box-office charts, comic panels only where no real image exists. Brand: black and warm gold.
audience: Adults 18–44 who follow movies, TV and celebrity news (US, UK, India). Not made for kids.
visual_style: Bold comic-book illustration, thick black ink outlines, halftone dots, black and warm gold palette with red accents, dramatic lighting.
script_rules: Hook in the first 2.5 seconds; 160-220 words; short spoken sentences; every fact sourced; exact quotes only; end with a question to the viewer.
publish_rules: Title under 60 characters with the surprising fact (e.g. "The Movie That Destroyed a Hollywood Studio"). Description: 2-line summary + full Sources and Image credits list. Hashtags: #hollywood #movies #shorts + 1-2 film-specific. Comments open (adult channel).

research.brief: True Hollywood stories with a twist: famous flops, studio near-collapses, on-set disasters, box-office upsets, origin stories of movie rules. Prefer stories with free-licence photos and solid sources. Avoid gossip, rumours and anything about minors.

notes: Pipeline reel v2 (26 Oct 2026): daily story finder (Wikipedia-grounded) → script → fact-check → Voicebox → shots → top-editor cut → QA → upload package. Anand uploads.

packaging.title_pattern: "The Movie That <shocking result>" / "Why <star/studio> <surprising action>" / "<Number> Hours/Dollars That <result>" — surprising fact first.
packaging.geo: USA, UK, Canada, Australia and India
